title: Night Architect passdown sketch
content:
Quick context
- I'm the night lead for the week (Aisha). This is a fast passdown for whoever takes 23:00-07:00. Not formal; just the stuff I found useful.
- Primary goals: keep hosted-api stable, keep latency SLOs, prevent noisy escalations to infra pager.

Current state summary
- No Sev active at the moment.
- 2 degraded routes (region-eu-west/model-rerank) showing higher 95p latency since ~03:00 UTC — likely due to a nightly heavy batching job that overlaps with small bursts from customer X.
- Dedicated pool-green: 84% GPU utilization, autoscale +1 triggered at 02:45 but took ~6m to stabilize.
- KV cache hit-rate for chat-conversations dropped to 61% during the 02:00 spike (baseline ~88%).

Things to check at start of shift (5–10m)
- Alert page: https://ops.redwood.ai/alerts -> filter "night" and "hosted-api"
- SLO dashboard: Console > Per-route > hosted-api > 95p latency (last 1h, last 24h)
- Dedicated pools: infra > capacity > pool-green (check queued requests)
- KV cache metrics: infra > caching (look for cache evictions and memory pressure)
- Recent deploys: github PRs merged in last 6h (if any deploys, watch for rollout canary)

Quick checks/commands (copy-paste)
- Tail latest logs for model-rerank errors (prod cluster):
  kubectl -n hosted-prod logs -l app=model-rerank --since=10m | sed -n '1,200p'
- Check queue depth for pool-green:
  curl -sS 'https://internal-api.redwood/infra/pools/pool-green/metrics' | jq '.queued_requests, .gpu_utilization'
- Inspect KV cache stats (redis cluster):
  redis-cli -c -h redis-prod-1 info all | egrep 'evicted_keys|used_memory_human|keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses'

Recent anomalies & quick notes
- 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC: short CPU thrashing on host-worker-13 after nightly model optimizer job started; auto-heal reboot happened and instance rejoined. Watch host-worker-13's boot_count (should be <=3).
- 2026-03-07: customer X increased batch size; recommended they switch to "burst" plan to avoid interfering with pooled autoscale. Raised INF-3421 to track follow-up.

Playbook snippets (for tonight)
- If 95p latency > 1200ms on hosted-api for >10m:
  1) Check recent deploys (if deploy in last 30m, rollback to previous and notify on #ops-night).
  2) If not deploy-related, identify top 3 slow routes: Console > Top Routes > 95p.
  3) For model-specific latency (e.g., rerank): temporarily route to quantized variant: 
     curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
          -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"rerank-quant-v2"}' \
          https://infra-router.redwood.local/route-switch
  4) If autoscale not keeping up, open paging to infra-oncall and attach pool metrics.

- If memory pressure on redis (cache) and evictions rising:
  - Scale read-replicas +1 (infra runbook -> redis scale), and enable temporary TTL on ephemeral keys: run key-scan script (in scripts/night)
  - Notify #platform-cache with snapshot of last 5m metrics

Escalation contacts (order)
1) Marcus Li (oncall infra) — pager: +1 555-0134, slack: @marcusli
2) Samira Khan (serving runtime) — slack: @samira, phone: +1 555-0199
3) PagerDuty Primary (if both unreachable) -> use PD escalation 

Open TODOs / follow-ups (for next day)
- Revisit model optimizer job schedule; move to 04:30 UTC to avoid the 02:00 peak (raise RFC).
- Add alert for KV cache hit-rate < 70% (threshold suggestion).
- Confirm with customer X re: batching patterns (INF-3421).

Notes to whoever inherits this shift
- If you see a consistent 5–10% latency uplift across multiple routes but no errors, check whether any background jobs are running (look at "night-ops-scheduled" tag in infra job list).
- Don't escalate immediately on a single CANARY failure — sometimes canaries flake. Wait for 3 consecutive failures within 5m or correlated errors on production routes.
- Keep the handoff message short in #ops-night with 3 bullets: current health, outstanding risks, and what you did during the shift. Example: "23:00-07:00: No Sevs; pool-green at 86% (watch autoscale); opened INF-3421 for customer X batching; moved canary -> quant-variant for rerank."

Sticky checks (if bored)
- Peek at token-cost dashboard -> any customer skyrocketing spend could indicate runaway loops.
- Quick audit: check PD recent alerts for reoccurring flaps (filter by service hosted-api)

Personal checklist (my habits)
- Coffee, log in to pager, check logs, ping Marcus if unsure, leave a 3-line handoff.

Unresolved questions / things I scribbled down
- Why did KV cache hit-rate drop specifically at 02:00? (suspect eviction due to optimizer job + larger ephemeral keys).
- Can we gate heavy nightly jobs behind a mutex that checks recent request rate? TODO: propose in infra-ops sync.

End of sketch — keep this ephemeral. If you make a permanent fix, please update the confluence runbook and move relevant steps to /product/ops/runbooks/night.
